method: S1 is the open RACGP AJGP 2024 anal fissure review, fetched and checked verbatim (32 claims). A1 is AMH, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED across the 'Perianal disorders' topic and the 'Glyceryl trinitrate (rectal)' and 'Anorectal products' monographs; no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, each claim carries its page's locator. FIRST GUIDELINE IN THIS CORPUS WITH QUOTED DOSES: 2 of the 5 dose-flagged claims come from S1 and carry a verbatim quote, so they are machine re-checkable and are NOT in the attestation queue; 3 come from A1 and are. Until now every dose in the corpus was licensed, so dose:true and 'unverifiable' were the same set by accident; verify.py now reports the two counts separately. S1 covers treatments AMH does not mention at all (topical calcium channel blockers, botulinum toxin); that is recorded as a coverage gap in A1, not as a disagreement.

claims.claim: Anal fissure is a superficial tear in the anoderm distal to the dentate line and is the second most common anorectal problem after haemorrhoids, affecting both genders equally
claims.source_text: Anal fissure (AF) is characterised by a superficial tear in the anoderm distal to the dentate line. 1,2 It is one of the most common anorectal problems presenting in healthcare settings, second only to haemorrhoids, and affects both genders equally.

claims.claim: Estimates of anal fissure frequency in the general population are 10 to 15%, although the actual number might be higher because patients do not present
claims.source_text: Estimates of AF frequency in the general population are 10-15%, although the actual number might be higher due to patients not presenting to healthcare providers.

claims.claim: A 2019 study of colorectal surgeons in Australia and New Zealand showed genuine clinical uncertainty in approximately two-thirds of clinical management questions about anal fissure
claims.source_text: Despite this prevalence, a 2019 study of colorectal surgeons in Australia and New Zealand showed genuine clinical uncertainty in approximately two-thirds of clinical management questions.

claims.claim: If medical treatments fail it is imperative to refer patients to a general or colorectal surgeon for further evaluation and treatment
claims.source_text: However, if medical treatments fail, it is imperative to refer patients on to a general or colorectal surgeon for further evaluation and treatment.

claims.claim: Anal fissure presents with severe tearing pain with defaecation often with spots of bright red blood, and the pain can persist for one to two hours or more, causing many patients to fear defaecation and worsen constipation
claims.source_text: Patients with AF will present with severe tearing pain with defaecation, often accompanied by spots of bright red blood. 2 This pain can persist for one to two hours or more afterwards, causing many patients to fear defaecation and worsen symptoms of constipation as a result.

claims.claim: Diagnosis is often achieved by visual inspection with the patient in the lateral decubitus position or prone flexed at the hips, gently parting the buttocks
claims.source_text: Definitive diagnosis is often achieved with visual inspection. The patient might lie in the lateral decubitus position or prone over a table flexed at the hips. Once in position, gentle parting of the buttocks might reveal the fissure.

claims.claim: Digital examination is contraindicated with suspected anal fissure because of the pain, and if a fissure is not apparent gently pressing on the anterior or posterior anal sphincter might produce the characteristic pain
claims.source_text: If a fissure is not apparent, gently pressing on the anterior or posterior anal sphincter might produce the characteristic pain. 5 Digital exam is contraindicated with suspected AF due to this pain.

claims.claim: Acute fissures are present for six weeks or less and appear as a fresh laceration, often heal spontaneously within 4 to 6 weeks or with medical management, although approximately 40% progress to chronic fissures
claims.source_text: Acute fissures present for six weeks or less are seen as a fresh laceration on the sphincter upon examination (Figure 1A,C). Acute AF often heals spontaneously within 4-6 weeks or with medical management, although approximately 40% will progress to chronic fissures.

claims.claim: Chronic fissures often have raised edges and exposed internal anal sphincter, with distal sentinel tags and hypertrophied anal papilla at the internal apex possibly present
claims.source_text: Chronic fissures often have raised edges and exposed internal anal sphincter (IAS). Distal sentinel tags and hypertrophied anal papilla at the internal apex might also be present

claims.claim: Anal fissure is thought to occur from localised ischaemia augmented by internal anal sphincter hypertonicity, which corresponds to 90% of presenting cases being in the posterior midline, an area receiving less than half the perfusion of the rest of the anal canal
claims.source_text: Data supports the idea that AF occurs due to localised ischaemia augmented by IAS hypertonicity. 8 This theory corresponds to the high prevalence of fissures in the posterior midline (90% of all presenting AF cases), an area that receives less than half of perfusion compared to the rest of the anal canal.

claims.claim: Primary anal fissure may be idiopathic but is often correlated with local trauma such as hard stools, prolonged diarrhoea, vaginal delivery or anal penetration, with acute injury triggering internal anal sphincter spasm and resting hypertonicity that reduces perfusion and hinders healing
claims.source_text: Primary AF might be idiopathic but is often correlated with local trauma, such as hard stools, prolonged diarrhoea, vaginal delivery or anal penetration. An acute injury can trigger spasms of the IAS, causing IAS resting hypertonicity. The resulting pressure on blood vessels supplying the area decreases perfusion, causing ischaemia and hindering healing of the fissure.

claims.claim: Most treatments focus on reducing internal anal sphincter resting tone, but fissures anterior to the midline are usually related to occult external sphincter injury, often lack internal anal sphincter hypertonicity, and require alternative treatment methods
claims.source_text: As a result, most treatments focus on reducing IAS resting tone. However, fissures anterior to the midline are usually related to occult external sphincter injury and often lack IAS hypertonicity. These fissures require alternative treatment methods.

claims.claim: Secondary anal fissure comprises less than 1% of presentations, is often characterised by multiple fissures or fissures off midline, and is associated with previous anal surgery, inflammatory bowel disease especially Crohn's disease, granulomatous diseases such as tuberculosis and sarcoidosis, and gastrointestinal malignancies
claims.source_text: Secondary AF, comprising less than 1% of AF presentations, is often characterised by multiple fissures or fissures off midline. 1 These fissures are associated with a variety of histories, including patients with previous anal surgeries, inflammatory bowel disease (especially Crohn's disease), granulomatous diseases (eg tuberculosis and sarcoidosis) and gastrointestinal malignancies (eg colon cancer).

claims.claim: Sexually transmissible infections might present with anal fissure in addition to discharge, perianal ulcers or fever, and if secondary anal fissure is suspected surgical therapies should be postponed pending further investigation and multidisciplinary involvement
claims.source_text: Sexually transmitted infections might also present with AF in addition to discharge, perianal ulcers or fever. If a secondary AF is suspected, surgical therapies should be postponed pending further investigation and multidisciplinary involvement.

claims.claim: Management should aim to reduce constipation, relieve pain and heal the fissure, minimising risk of sepsis, fistula formation and chronic fissure development
claims.source_text: Management should aim to reduce constipation, relieve pain and heal the fissure. Risk of complications, including sepsis, fistula formation and chronic fissure development, should be minimised.

claims.claim: The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons guidelines suggest increased fibre intake, sitz baths and if necessary stool softeners as first-line therapy for acute anal fissure or for chronic anal fissure in patients who elect or are unable to have surgery
claims.source_text: The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons (ASCRS) guidelines suggest a combination of increased fibre intake, sitz baths and, if necessary, stool softeners as the first-line therapy for acute AF or chronic AF in patients who elect or are unable to have surgery.

claims.claim: Conservative therapy has shown a healing rate of 87% with 15 g per day of fibre supplementation, reducing recurrence to 16% versus 68% with placebo
claims.source_text: Conservative therapy has shown a healing rate of 87% with 15 g/day of fibre supplementation. This therapy reduced recurrence at 16% versus 68% with placebo.

claims.claim: Glyceryl trinitrate ointment undergoes cellular metabolism to release nitric oxide which relaxes the internal anal sphincter by acting as an inhibitory neurotransmitter
claims.source_text: GTN undergoes cellular metabolism to release nitric oxide, which relaxes the IAS by acting as an inhibitory neurotransmitter.

claims.claim: A Cochrane review compared glyceryl trinitrate to placebo and found it slightly but significantly better at 49% versus 37% with P less than 0.004, although recurrence was widespread at over 50%
claims.source_text: A Cochrane review compared GTN to placebo and found GTN to be slightly but significantly better (49% vs 37%, P <0.004), although recurrence was widespread (>50%).

claims.claim: A randomised controlled trial found co-administration of glyceryl trinitrate and topical metronidazole decreased pain with defecation early and significantly increased healing by the end of week 6, at 97.1% versus 85.2% with glyceryl trinitrate alone
claims.source_text: A randomised control trial performed by Sahid et al found that co-administration of GTN and topical metronidazole decreased pain with defection during the early stages of treatment and significantly increased healing of AF by the end of week 6 (97.1% vs 85.2% with GTN alone, P <0.014).

claims.claim: Significant side effects of glyceryl trinitrate include headaches, light-headedness and local irritation, and their severity causes up to 20% of patients to discontinue therapy
claims.source_text: Significant side effects include headaches, light-headedness and local irritation. The severity of these side effects causes up to 20% of patients to discontinue therapy.

claims.claim: Topical calcium channel blockers relax the internal anal sphincter by blocking calcium influx to the cytoplasm of smooth muscle cells, and ASCRS guidelines recommend them when glyceryl trinitrate therapy has failed
claims.source_text: Topical calcium channel blockers (CCBs) relax the IAS by blocking calcium influx to the cytoplasm of smooth muscle cells. 1 ASCRS guidelines recommend CCB when GTN therapy has failed.

claims.claim: The two most used topical calcium channel blockers are nifedipine 0.2 to 0.5% gel and diltiazem 2% cream
claims.source_text: The two most used CCBs are topical nifedipine (0.2-0.5% gel) and diltiazem (2% cream).

claims.claim: Calcium channel blockers are as effective as glyceryl trinitrate and are favoured in patients with poor reactions to it because adverse effect rates are much lower with only some experiencing mild headaches and anal pruritus, with reported healing rates varying from 65% to 96%
claims.source_text: CCBs have been shown to be as effective as GTN and are favoured for patients with poor reactions to GTN, as reported adverse effect rates are much lower, with only some experiencing mild headaches and anal pruritis. 1,3 Reported healing rates vary from 65% to 96%.

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin A prevents acetylcholine release from presynaptic terminals causing relaxation of both the external and internal anal sphincter for up to three months, and ASCRS guidelines recommend it when topical therapy has failed
claims.source_text: Botulinum toxin A (BTA) is produced by Clostridium botulinum and acts as an inhibitory neurotransmitter by preventing acetylcholine release from presynaptic terminals. This causes relaxation of both the external and IAS for up to three months. 1 ASCRS guidelines recommend BTA when topical therapy has failed.

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin is strongly recommended in patients at high risk of developing incontinence from surgery including those with Crohn's disease or a history of anal surgery, with adverse effects including short-term incontinence but at lower rates than surgical methods
claims.source_text: It is strongly recommended in patients at high risk of developing incontinence from surgery, including those with Crohn's disease or a history of anal surgery. 3 Adverse effects include short-term incontinence but at lower rates than surgical methods.

claims.claim: One prospective study showed comparable healing rates between glyceryl trinitrate, diltiazem and botulinum toxin of nearly 55%, with diltiazem and botulinum toxin having lower reported adverse effects than glyceryl trinitrate, and long-term recurrence might be up to 42% depending on method
claims.source_text: One prospective study showed comparable healing rates between GTN, diltiazem and BTA of nearly 55%. Additionally, diltiazem and BTA had lower reported adverse effects than GTN. 4 Long-term recurrence might be up to 42%, depending on method.

claims.claim: Surgical management of anal fissure is typically recommended at least 6 to 8 weeks after attempting conservative treatment, although it might be first-line if the fissure is hyperalgesic or infected, and the best results are seen with a combination of surgical and medical management
claims.source_text: Surgical management of AF is typically recommended at least 6-8 weeks after attempting conservative treatment, although it might be the first-line treatment if the fissure is hyperalgesic or infected. The best results are seen with a combination of surgical and medical management.

claims.claim: Lateral internal sphincterotomy is most often used for chronic anal fissure and consists of a partial incision to the internal anal sphincter to relieve hypertonia
claims.source_text: Lateral internal sphincterotomy (LIS) is most often used for managing chronic AF. 8 This procedure consists of a partial incision to the IAS to relieve hypertonia.

claims.claim: The significant adverse effect of lateral internal sphincterotomy is transient incontinence of flatus or stool in up to 17% of patients, with 1% experiencing faecal incontinence five years after the procedure
claims.source_text: The significant adverse effect of this procedure is transient incontinence of flatus or stool in up to 17% of patients, with 1% experiencing faecal incontinence five years after the procedure.

claims.claim: A Cochrane review favoured lateral internal sphincterotomy in uncomplicated hypertonic anal fissure but recommended combination fissurectomy with advancement anoplasty in patients with hypotonia, diagnostic doubt, or high risk of faecal incontinence
claims.source_text: A Cochrane review favoured LIS in uncomplicated hypertonic AF cases but recommended combination fissurectomy/advancement anoplasty in AF patients with hypotonia when there is diagnostic doubt or if there is high risk for faecal incontinence with LIS.

claims.claim: Non-surgical management should be attempted for at least 6 to 8 weeks and chronic anal fissure should be treated with a combination of medical and surgical management
claims.source_text: - Non-surgical management should be attempted for at least 6-8 weeks. - Chronic AF should be treated with a combination of medical and surgical management.
